blocks.heading: Best Career for My Child
rows: Fit
Does the daily work match how your child naturally works and thinks?
Your child can describe a normal Tuesday in that role without dread.
Affordability
Can the family fund this path without a loan the child cannot realistically repay?
The plan survives a bad-case scenario, not only the best case.
Demand
Do real employers, clients, or exams currently reward this skill?
Internships, entry roles, or apprenticeships genuinely exist for it.
AI-resistance
Does the role still need judgment, trust, or hands-on skill that AI cannot fully replace?
Your child can name what a human still does better than a tool in that field.

blocks.heading: Actually Looks Like After 12th Right Now
rows: Science (PCM)
Engineering, data and analytics, cybersecurity, architecture, defense services, applied research
Roughly Rs 3-8 LPA for most colleges; Rs 10-12+ LPA is realistic mainly from top-tier institutes or product-based roles
Science (PCB)
Medicine, nursing, physiotherapy, pharmacy, biotechnology, allied health, health-tech and health-communication roles
Roughly Rs 3-7 LPA to start in most allied-health and pharma roles; medicine has a much longer, costlier runway before income begins
Commerce
CA, CS, actuarial science, financial risk management, banking, business analytics, digital marketing, entrepreneurship
CA and finance-credentialed roles often start around Rs 8-15 LPA in metro hubs; general B.Com without a credential trends much lower
Arts / Humanities
Law, psychology, design, journalism and mass communication, civil services, public policy, UX research, hotel management
Wide range depending on specialisation and proof of work; law and design with a strong portfolio can match or beat many commerce paths
Skill-first / diploma
Applied trades, digital skills, design tools, no-code building, technical certifications, apprenticeship-linked roles
Highly variable, but often faster time-to-first-income than a 3-4 year degree, especially with a visible project or client result

blocks.heading: Exam Math Most Families Never Run
rows: NEET (MBBS)
~23 lakh registered
~1.1 lakh MBBS seats nationwide
Under 5% get an MBBS seat
JEE Main (IIT/NIT)
~15.4 lakh unique candidates
~17,800 IIT + ~24,000 NIT seats
Under 4% land an IIT or NIT seat
CUET (various UG courses)
~13 lakh registered
~2.5 lakh seats across participating universities
Roughly 15-20% success ratio, notably better than JEE or NEET

figures.source: No. NEET 2026 had roughly 23 lakh candidates competing for about 1.1 lakh MBBS seats, and JEE Main pass rates for IIT/NIT seats sit under 4%. Most 12th-pass students in India were never going to get one of these seats by definition of the ratio alone. Strong, well-paid careers exist across commerce, design, healthcare-adjacent roles, government exams, skilled trades, and digital-skill paths that do not run through JEE or NEET at all.

blocks.heading: One Core Skill That Matches the Target

items.text: One core skill that matches the target field, built with enough depth to be usable, not just a certificate.
One multiplier skill on top, communication, basic data or AI-tool fluency, or business sense, that makes the core skill more valuable.
Visible proof of work: a project, a portfolio piece, an internship result, or a small paid task a stranger can actually see.
Market positioning: knowing which employers or clients actually pay for this skill combination, not guessing.
Leading with "everyone in the family does X" instead of the child's actual fit.
Comparing your child to a cousin or neighbour's child who "settled down well."
Treating any hesitation about a "safe" field as ingratitude.
Bringing up money only as a threat, never as a shared planning exercise.
Deciding privately, then presenting it as the only real option.

blocks.heading: Tests Without Treating Them As a Verdict

items.text: Surface consistent interest and work-style patterns your child may not have named out loud.
Narrow a confusing list of 10-15 options down to a shortlist of 3-4.
Give the family a neutral third input, reducing pure opinion-based arguments.

blocks.heading: Conversation Families Avoid Until It's Too Late

items.text: Can your child name one specific target role this course leads to, not just "a good future".
Is the projected EMI realistic against the likely starting salary for that role, not the best-case one.
Does the family still have a buffer if the first job search after graduation takes longer than expected.
Has your child done any small project, internship, or proof of interest in this field already.
If the interest rate or fee structure changes, does the plan still hold.
World Economic Forum on how core job skills and entry-level hiring are shifting through 2030.
Wheebox India Skills Report on national employability and AI-driven hiring trends.
Government of India on NEP 2020's multidisciplinary and multiple entry-exit structure in higher education.
Peer-reviewed research on parental pressure, academic stress, and adolescent well-being around entrance exams in India.
National Education Policy 2020 official reference for structure and implementation timelines.
Government-recognised career and job services portal for India.
